newsitem.title: CANADA: Trizec shareholders vote for merger.
newsitem.headline: Trizec shareholders vote for merger.

text.p: Trizec Corp Ltd on Thursday said its shareholders approved the proposed merger of Trizec and Horsham Corp.
The proposed merger, which is still subject to various final approvals, will create a real estate company to be called Trizec Hahn Corp, Trizec said.
Trizec, which is based in Toronto, said over 99 percent of the votes cast by shareholders were in favor of the merger.
The company said of the minority shareholdings, which excludes shares owned by Horsham, over 98 percent were voted in favor of the merger.
Trizec said more than 86 percent of the total issued and outstanding common shares were voted.
Under the terms of the merger, which was announced September 10, Trizec shareholders other than Horsham will received 0.58 of a subordinate voting share of Trizec Hahn for each Trizec common shares.

The merger, which was designed to boost Horsham's stock price, will create one of North America's largest publicly traded real estate companies with about US$6 billion in assets and a real estate porfolio valued at about US$3.5 billion.
Trizec shares were unchanged at C$13.70 in early afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Horsham shares fell C$0.15 to C$23.30.
